2023_015_8_b_24680_troy_school_district_.paragraph: Troy School District's Federal Awards Supplemental Information for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2023 assembles the single audit package required by the Uniform Guidance: three independent auditor's reports, the Schedule of Expenditures of Federal Awards, a reconciliation of financial statement federal revenue to that schedule, explanatory notes, and the Schedule of Findings and Questioned Costs. Federal expenditures for the year totaled $13,844,823 against award amounts of $39,076,556 shown for memo purposes only. The auditor, in reports dated October 3, 2023, expressed unmodified opinions on compliance for each major federal program, identified no material weaknesses, significant deficiencies, or audit findings, and reported that the district qualified as a low-risk auditee.

Overview
Federal Awards Supplemental Information of Troy School District for the year ended June 30, 2023, presented to the Board of Education. All auditor's reports carry the date October 3, 2023, the same date as the report on the district's basic financial statements, which contained unmodified opinions.

Auditor's Reports Included
- Report on Schedule of Expenditures of Federal Awards Required by the Uniform Guidance (page 1): the schedule and the reconciliation are fairly stated in all material respects in relation to the financial statements as a whole.
- Report on Internal Control Over Financial Reporting and on Compliance and Other Matters under Government Auditing Standards (pages 2-3): no material weaknesses identified; tests disclosed no instances of noncompliance required to be reported.
- Report on Compliance for Each Major Federal Program and Report on Internal Control Over Compliance Required by the Uniform Guidance (pages 4-6): unmodified opinion on compliance; no material weaknesses in internal control over compliance identified.

Type of auditor's report issued: unmodified. No material weaknesses, no significant deficiencies, and no material noncompliance were identified for either the financial statements or the major programs; no findings were required to be reported under 2 CFR 200.516(a). 2023_015_8_b_24680_troy_school_district_.verbose:
Federal Awards Supplemental Information for Troy School District covering the fiscal year ended June 30, 2023, prepared for the Board of Education and presented to the board on the October 17, 2023 agenda as item 8.B.

Contents. The package comprises the Report on Schedule of Expenditures of Federal Awards Required by the Uniform Guidance (page 1); the Report on Internal Control Over Financial Reporting and on Compliance and Other Matters Based on an Audit of Financial Statements Performed in Accordance with Government Auditing Standards (pages 2-3); the Report on Compliance for Each Major Federal Program and Report on Internal Control Over Compliance Required by the Uniform Guidance (pages 4-6); the Schedule of Expenditures of Federal Awards (pages 7-10); the Reconciliation of Basic Financial Statements Federal Revenue with Schedule of Expenditures of Federal Awards (page 11); Notes to Schedule of Expenditures of Federal Awards (page 12); and the Schedule of Findings and Questioned Costs (page 13).

Auditor's reports. All three reports are dated October 3, 2023, the same date as the report on the basic financial statements of the governmental activities, each major fund, and the aggregate remaining fund information, which contained unmodified opinions. The auditor states that no procedures were performed with respect to the audited financial statements subsequent to October 3, 2023, and that in its opinion the schedule of expenditures of federal awards and the reconciliation are fairly stated in all material respects in relation to the financial statements as a whole. Under Government Auditing Standards, the auditor did not identify any deficiencies in internal control considered to be material weaknesses, and tests of compliance with provisions of laws, regulations, contracts, and grant agreements disclosed no instances of noncompliance or other matters required to be reported. On major program compliance, the auditor concluded that the School District complied, in all material respects, with the compliance requirements identified in the OMB Compliance Supplement that could have a direct and material effect on each major federal program for the year ended June 30, 2023, and identified no material weaknesses in internal control over compliance. The audit was conducted under generally accepted auditing standards, Government Auditing Standards issued by the Comptroller General of the United States, and Title 2 U.S. Code of Federal Regulations Part 200.

2023_016_5_g_es35112_troy_school_distric.paragraph: Quote ES35112 from A+ Technology and Security Solutions, Inc., dated October 10, 2023, proposes supplying Troy School District with two AXIS Camera Station S1296 Rack 96 TB recording servers, manufacturer part number 02542-001, at $16,809.18 each. The quoted total is $33,618.36 with sales tax of $0.00, priced under PEPPM Purchasing Cooperative contract #533902-176 at the customer's request. The quote also lists optional lease payments ranging from $1,106.04 for 36 months to $658.92 for 72 months, and standard terms including a 50 percent deposit requirement and a 30-day validity window.

Sales quote number ES35112 dated 10/10/2023, titled Troy School District - Axis Server quote request - PEPPM pricing, prepared by sales representative Sean Atkinson of A+ Technology and Security Solutions, Inc. The vendor is licensed by the NYS Department of State, license #12000298891. Bill To is Michelle McKay, Troy School District, 4420 Livernois Road, Troy MI 48098. Ship To is Beth Soggs at the same address. Each of the four pages is time-stamped Oct 10, 2023 3:34:58 PM.

Product Description
The AXIS Camera Station S1296 Rack 96 TB is described as an out-of-the-box ready recording server validated for ultra high-definition recording, preconfigured and preloaded with AXIS Camera Station video management software including licenses for 96 devices plus all necessary software. Configuration can be imported from AXIS Site Designer, and the AXIS Recorder Toolbox installation wizard is cited for quick setup. Features listed include redundant enterprise-grade hard drives and power supplies, the operating system stored on a solid-state drive with built-in operating system recovery, and a FIPS 140-2 compliant TPM providing encryption of data at rest. A 5-year limited hardware warranty with on-site hardware replacement and keep-your-hard-drive services is included.

Scope of Work
A+ Technology and Security Solutions proposes to supply the Axis hardware, specifically (2) AXIS Camera Station S1296 Rack 96 TB (02542-001), to Troy School District (MI), with pricing provided according to the PEPPM Purchasing Cooperative as requested by the customer under contract #533902-176. Signature and print name lines are provided for acknowledgment of the scope of work, assumptions, notes, and customer expectations.

Optional Leasing

| Term | Payment |
|---|---|
| Total price | $33,618.36 |
| 36 month lease | $1,106.04 |
| 48 month lease | $877.44 |
| 60 month lease | $736.24 |
| 72 month lease | $658.92 |

Lease payments are described as guidelines only, subject to credit approval, with actual payment determined at time of approval.

Key Terms and Conditions
Proposals are valid for 30 days from the date listed, a limitation attributed to supply chain shortages and material price increases. Overdue undisputed progress payments allow the seller to suspend work and claim interest at an annual rate of 18 percent or the maximum permitted by the State of New York. Cancellation or suspension triggers an adjustment charge equal to all invoices for work performed and hardware delivered plus 15 percent. Returns require items in new, unused, resellable condition in original packaging, returned within 30 days of order, and may carry a 25 percent restocking fee; refused returns may incur a $125.00 test and inspection charge. Warranty claims require written notice of failure within ninety days after installation. The agreement is governed by New York law and becomes binding upon written acceptance by an authorized customer representative and receipt of a 50 percent deposit, after which progress payments are invoiced based on percentage of job completion. Walkthroughs occur during normal business hours of 8am to 5pm Monday through Friday, with overtime, premium, and holiday rates otherwise. Invoice payment is due within thirty days of receipt.

Terms and conditions. (2) Proposals: based on straight-time labor, with overtime requested by the customer treated as an extra; the proposal expires 30 days after date received. (3) Progress payments: all equipment delivered directly to the job site or received at the seller's offices for configuration is billed upon receipt; the seller may invoice as work progresses; if the customer becomes overdue on any undisputed progress payment, the seller may suspend work and is entitled to interest at an annual rate of 18 percent or the maximum permitted by the State of New York, plus other legal remedies. (6) Taxes: any sales, use, occupancy, excise, or other federal, state, or local tax the seller must pay is added to invoices and paid by the customer. 2023_017_student_friendly_character.paragraph: Character | Student-Friendly Deep Learning Progression is a two-page rubric written in first-person student language, describing growth in the Character competency across four dimensions and five levels of evidence. The stated aim is learning to deep learn, to keep trying, to have integrity, empathy, and compassion, and to always be a learner. The material is credited to Copyright 2019 by Education in Motion (New Pedagogies for Deep Learning), with reproduction authorized for educational use by educators, local school sites, and noncommercial or nonprofit entities that have purchased the book.
2023_017_student_friendly_character.page:
What It Is
A student-facing learning progression for the Character competency, part of a Learning Progressions series. The header describes Character as learning to deep learn, to keep trying, to have integrity, empathy, and compassion, and to always be a learner. It runs across two pages, the second labeled Character (Cont'd).

Structure
Four dimensions are each described at five levels: Limited Evidence, Emerging, Developing, Accelerating, and Proficient. Every descriptor is written as an I statement for student self-assessment.

| Dimension | Page |
|---|---|
| Proactive stance toward life and learning to deep learn | 1 |
| Grit, tenacity, perseverance, and resilience | 1 |
| Empathy, compassion, and integrity | 2 |
| Using technology for learning (leveraging digital) | 2 |

Proactive Stance Toward Life and Learning to Deep Learn
At Limited Evidence the student is not clear about what needs to be learned or why, can complete teacher-prepared tasks but needs help reflecting, and does not yet find learning a positive experience. Emerging adds identifying with help what is known and needed, choosing a topic and finding information with help, beginning to see peer and teacher feedback as opportunities, and believing learning and achievement are possible. Developing describes interests, knowledge, and learning needs, creating or designing a project, using feedback to improve, and experiencing learning as positive and leading to accomplishment. Accelerating adds skill at working out how to learn, reflecting on progress, seeking feedback, applying learning to current and future projects, and balancing work with play. Proficient describes finding and creating one's own learning opportunities, continually building knowledge and skills for success in life, creating meaningful solutions that impact life and the world, and actively seeking feedback even when challenging.

Grit, Tenacity, Perseverance, and Resilience
Limited Evidence describes usually giving up when facing unexpected challenges or negative feedback and being unable to work through hard tasks. Emerging describes needing a lot of support with setbacks and beginning to work through challenges with encouragement. Developing describes learning to persevere, being thrown off track by major setbacks sometimes but handling small or medium challenges by pausing, reflecting, adapting, and finding new solutions. Accelerating describes persevering and never giving up on the most challenging tasks, and working through major setbacks or negative feedback. Proficient describes grit, tenacity, perseverance, adaptability, and resilience that allow the student to work through any challenge and help others do the same, and understanding character qualities as essential to creating meaningful change.

Empathy, Compassion, and Integrity
Progresses from being unsure what others feel, to beginning to put oneself in others' shoes, to imagining how others experience the world and wanting to be courageous about doing the right thing, to regularly reflecting on feeling more empathy and showing more compassion as an authentic goal, to regularly modeling compassion, empathy, and integrity even when unnoticed or inconvenient, with sincerity, fairness, trustworthiness, and bravery as valued virtues.

Using Technology for Learning (Leveraging Digital)
Progresses from using some digital without seeing how it supports learning, to occasional use and beginning to use digital to develop empathy, compassion, and grit, to regular use with understanding of how digital deepens those traits, to explaining how digital helps learning and reflection, to effortless use throughout the learning experience and using digital to support others by encouraging them and providing feedback.

Attribution
Source line on both pages: Copyright 2019 by Education in Motion (New Pedagogies for Deep Learning). All rights reserved. Reproduction authorized for educational use by educators, local school sites, and noncommercial or nonprofit entities that have purchased the book.
2023_017_student_friendly_character.verbose:
Character | Student-Friendly Deep Learning Progression, a two-page rubric distributed with the Troy School District Board of Education materials for the meeting of October 3, 2023, under the file name student-friendly-Character. It belongs to a series headed Learning Progressions and is written entirely in first-person student voice so that students can locate their own practice on the scale.

Framing statement. The subtitle on both pages reads: Learning to deep learn, to keep trying, to have integrity, empathy, and compassion, and to always be a learner.

Architecture. The rubric is a matrix. Rows are dimensions of the Character competency; columns are five levels of evidence, labeled Limited Evidence, Emerging, Developing, Accelerating, and Proficient. Page one covers two dimensions, Proactive stance toward life and learning to deep learn, and Grit, tenacity, perseverance, and resilience. Page two, headed Character (Cont'd) | Student-Friendly Deep Learning Progression, repeats the dimension and level headers and covers Empathy, compassion, and integrity, and Using technology for learning (leveraging digital).

Dimension 1: Proactive stance toward life and learning to deep learn. Limited Evidence: the student is not clear about what needs to be learned and why; can complete tasks the teacher prepares but needs help to reflect on and understand how a task is going; learning is not yet a positive experience. Emerging: with help, the student can identify what is known, what needs to be learned, and why; with help, can choose a topic and find needed information; is learning to see peer and teacher feedback as opportunities to learn and improve; believes learning and achievement are possible. Developing: the student can describe interests, existing knowledge, learning needs, and reasons for learning; can choose a topic and create or design a project to support learning; listens to peer and teacher feedback and uses it to improve how learning happens; experiences learning as positive, leading to a feeling of accomplishment and achievement. Accelerating: the student understands what needs to be learned and is skilled at working out how to learn it; reflects on progress and seeks feedback while learning; uses what is learned to improve current and future projects; enjoys learning as a way to improve life; tries to balance work with play. Proficient: the student has the skills to find and create personal learning opportunities; is continually building knowledge and skills for success in life; creates meaningful solutions that impact both personal life and the world; actively seeks out feedback and uses it to better understand how learning happens and what supports growth; looks for any opportunity to learn something new even when it is challenging; balances work with play.

Dimension 2: Grit, tenacity, perseverance, and resilience. Limited Evidence: the student usually gives up when facing an unexpected challenge or receiving negative feedback, and when a task or experience is too hard is unable to work through the challenge to find a solution. Emerging: the student needs a lot of support to deal with setbacks, negative feedback, and difficult challenges, and is starting to work through challenges but still needs support and encouragement not to give up. Developing: the student is learning to persevere and not give up even when tasks are challenging; major setbacks or difficulties may throw the student off track sometimes, but small or medium challenges can be handled by pausing, reflecting, adapting, and finding new solutions. Accelerating: the student perseveres and never gives up, even on the most challenging tasks; when faced with major setbacks or negative feedback, pauses, reflects, adapts, and works through the challenge to find a solution; understands and can talk about why the character qualities matter for life. Proficient: grit, tenacity, perseverance, adaptability, and resilience allow the student to work through any challenge or setback and to help others do the same; the student seeks out feedback and uses it to help learning; and understands that the character qualities are essential for creating meaningful change in personal life and in the world.

Dimension 3: Empathy, compassion, and integrity. Limited Evidence: the student is not sure what other people might feel when interacting with them or when hearing about issues happening in the world. Emerging: the student is beginning to put himself or herself in others' shoes and can sometimes see what their experiences must be like. Developing: more and more, the student can imagine how others experience the world even without having experienced those things personally; would like to be courageous about doing the right thing in class and beyond it; wants to develop empathy, compassion, and integrity in order to be a better person. Accelerating: the student regularly reflects on how to feel more empathy and show more compassion for others, describing this as an authentic personal goal, and strives to be courageous within the class and beyond it. Proficient: the student regularly shows and models compassion, empathy, and integrity even when no one notices or when it is inconvenient; virtues such as sincerity, fairness, trustworthiness, and bravery matter and are how the student wishes others to describe both the person and the work produced.

Dimension 4: Using technology for learning (leveraging digital). Limited Evidence: the student uses some digital during the learning process but does not see how it supports learning. Emerging: the student uses digital to assist with learning occasionally and is beginning to use digital to develop empathy, compassion, and grit. Developing: the student regularly uses digital to support learning and understands how digital can deepen traits like empathy, compassion, and grit. Accelerating: the student knows and can explain how digital helps with learning, reflection, and developing traits like empathy, compassion, and grit. Proficient: the student effortlessly uses technology throughout the learning experience and uses digital to support others with their learning by encouraging them and providing feedback.

Attribution and permissions. Both pages carry the identical source line: Copyright 2019 by Education in Motion (New Pedagogies for Deep Learning). All rights reserved. Reproduction authorized for educational use by educators, local school sites, and/or noncommercial or nonprofit entities that have purchased the book. No Troy School District author, department, or presenter is named in the document itself, and it contains no figures, dollar amounts, dates other than the copyright year, or board action language.
